members.name: M.Thanusikan
members.reconciliation: The submitted routine-assistance description and 85-to-25 urgency change match the older M2-D01/M2-D02 examples. The supplied personal run uses M2-C01/M2-C02: both incidents are the same High-priority flood, both scores are 85, and two shelters remain. The summary below corrects the distinction; the member should review these corrections before the viva.

answers.What input changed?: Medical stock increased from 20 to 50 and available vehicles from one to three. Food stayed at 100. Shelter 1 remained 10/10; shelter 2 changed from 30/100 to 100/100. The same High-priority flood incident remained in both inputs.
answers.What was expected?: For this executed pair, the evidence-aligned expectation is that stock deficits clear and no shelter is selected, while urgency stays 85. The supplied expectation of lower urgency belongs to the older D-series pair, not this C-series run.
answers.What actually happened?: Both scenarios passed. Urgency was 85 in both. The original output selected shelter 2 and showed a medical deficit. The changed output returned nearest_shelter=null and all three resource-deficiency flags false.
answers.Which assertion or business rule explain: The checks assert urgency_score=85, nearest_shelter=null, and false deficit flags after the change. Medical 50, food 100 and three vehicles meet the current baselines. Full shelters are excluded; eligible shelters are ranked by available capacity, not geographic distance.

members.name: Denesh N
members.reconciliation: The supplied explanation matches the personal run. Its submitted table labels D-series examples; the screenshot and dated comparison use M3-C01/M3-C02. The summary adds the observed High-priority requirement rule for clarity.

answers.What input changed?: Priority changed from Medium to High, with available resources and volunteers each changing from one to zero. The input retained its explicit one-vehicle requirement.
answers.What was expected?: The supplied expectation is an empty allocation, reported shortages and REVISE, while human approval remains required.
answers.What actually happened?: Both scenarios passed. The original output allocated a response van, returned no gaps and APPROVE. The changed output allocated nothing, reported gaps of two Vehicles, two Medical resources and two Personnel, and returned REVISE. Human approval remained true.
answers.Which assertion or business rule explain: The checks assert empty/nonempty allocation and gap lists, requires_human_approval=true, and APPROVE/REVISE. In the current implementation, High priority replaces the explicit input requirement with the priority-based estimate. This comparison changes both priority and availability; it does not isolate their individual effects.

members.name: Deneshkar. P
members.reconciliation: The prior supplied explanation is preserved verbatim in Understanding_Submitted_20261008.md. The following four-part summary combines it with the verified M4-C01/M4-C02 personal run. It is not a new verbatim statement.

answers.What input changed?: Only the proposed shift start changed, from 10:00 to 09:30 UTC. The existing shift stayed 09:00-10:00, the proposed end stayed 11:00 and the volunteer remained available.
answers.What was expected?: The previously supplied explanation identifies adjacent shifts as non-overlapping and the 09:30 start as a 30-minute conflict requiring revision.
answers.What actually happened?: Both personal scenarios passed. The adjacent case returned is_valid=true and APPROVE. The changed case returned is_valid=false, REVISE and V2_DOUBLE_BOOKING.
answers.Which assertion or business rule explain: The checks assert those returned fields. Half-open intervals overlap when new_start < existing_end and existing_start < new_end. Equality at 10:00 is allowed. V2_DOUBLE_BOOKING is revisable; an agent recommendation does not itself approve the dispatch.
